_about: Callers for relay-sim.js. persona: who the caller is and how they behave. opening: exact first line (optional). expect.outcome: completed | transfer | any. expect.fields: loose checks on what Ava stored (substring, case-insensitive; phone compares digits; null = must be empty). Options: split (true = every second caller turn arrives as two turns with a pause; 'all' = every turn), splitGapMs, interruptRecap (caller cuts into the read-back with this line), dtmfAt (caller turn number at which 0 is pressed), hangupAt (caller turn number at which the line drops), silentFirstMs (caller says nothing at first). noise ('light' | 'heavy' | 'tv': what a bad line, an accent or a television does to the transcript Ava receives), silentAt ({turn, ms}: the caller goes quiet mid-call), neverSpeaks (a pocket dial).
callerRules: You are role-playing a person who has phoned RSE Energy Group, a heating, cooling and generator company in New Jersey. The other party is Ava, the company's phone assistant. You are the CALLER and only the caller. Reply with only the words you say out loud, the way a speech-to-text transcript would show them: no quotation marks, no stage directions, no emojis, no labels. Keep to one or two short sentences per turn unless your character says otherwise. Answer the question you were asked; do not volunteer details that were not asked for unless your character says to. Never act as the assistant, never offer help, never ask Ava what she needs. Do not repeat Ava's question back to her. If Ava reads your details back and they are right, confirm briefly; if something is wrong, say what is wrong. If you see a note in parentheses about silence, react the way a real caller would (for example: Hello? Are you still there?). When Ava has said goodbye, or the call is clearly over, reply with exactly [hangup]. If your character decides to end the call, say your last words, and on your next turn reply exactly [hangup].
